entities.summary:
Arnail François, marquis de Jaucourt, born in Paris in 1757, was a prominent French aristocrat and politician whose career spanned the tumultuous transition from the Ancien Régime through the French Revolution, the Napoleonic Empire, and the Bourbon Restoration, enduring until his death in 1852. A consistent advocate for constitutional monarchy and liberal ideals, Jaucourt served in various high-level capacities, reflecting the adaptability and resilience required to navigate nearly seven decades of profound political upheaval in Western Europe. His enduring presence in French statecraft, from the Legislative Assembly of 1791 to the Chamber of Peers under Louis XVIII, underscores his significance as a witness and participant in the fundamental reshaping of French society and governance.

Jaucourt's political journey began as a deputy for Seine-et-Marne to the Legislative Assembly in 1791, where he aligned with the Feuillants, supporting a constitutional monarchy. Imprisoned during the Reign of Terror, he later resumed public life under the Consulate and Empire, becoming a Senator in 1803 and a Count of the Empire in 1808. Crucially, during the First Restoration, Jaucourt played a pivotal role as Minister of State and as an ambassador to Prussia (1814) and Sardinia (1815). He was instrumental in the drafting of the Charter of 1814, a foundational document for the restored monarchy, and later presided over the Chamber of Peers from 1817 to 1823, helping to stabilize the post-Napoleonic political landscape.
